A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Agent World Model work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original environment-synthesis statistics, agent evaluations on three benchmarks, and verification, history-management, and scaling analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds generator comparisons, difficulty analyses, repeated judge evaluations, and code-similarity measurements.

M1.justification: The synthesis pipeline, history-aware GRPO, and reward equations are retained. However, new Table 13 calls the actual RL reward signal binary, while Equation 1 and Appendix A.5 still specify partial-completion reward 0.1. The PDFs do not resolve whether this is a caption error or an actual reward change.

E1.justification: Both versions cover the same AWM scenarios and tasks, BFCLv3, verified tau2-bench, and MCP-Universe. New analyses stratify existing tasks or vary generator and judge models; they do not establish new task requirements or domains. Workflow and user-management scenarios were already represented in v1.

E2.justification: Figure 4 newly includes EnvScaler in the environment-scaling comparison at 191 environments, using scores already reported in Table 4. v1's scaling figure contained only AWM. The comparator membership in the main benchmark and environment-quality tables remains unchanged.

E3.justification: v3 adds a 191-environment training condition, synthesis evaluation with three generators on 100 environments/1,000 tasks, complexity-stratified evaluations, and structural/lexical code-similarity protocols. These substantially expand the evaluation design. The retained benchmark settings and Appendix A hyperparameters are unchanged; the new MCP-adapter explanation was already documented in v1's appendix.

E4.justification: New analyses examine generator dependence, benchmark gains by difficulty, synthesized-task difficulty and unsolved training tasks, judge repeatability, and code-level diversity. Figure 4 also adds a comparison at matched environment counts. Existing verification, history-management, format-reward ablations, and verification case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Tables 10 and 13 introduce one substantial reliability study: 100 sampled 8B-agent trajectories judged five times by each of three models, with self-consistency, pairwise agreement, Fleiss' kappa, and reward-flip rates under binary and four-class coding. Existing four-run tau2-bench averaging and environment-quality uncertainty reporting remain unchanged; additional training seeds are not reported.

E6.justification: v3 adds substantial difficulty, generator, reliability, and code-diversity results in Tables 5, 7–8, 10, and 13–14, plus AWM results at 191 environments. Table 4 changes AWM-4B BFCLv3 Multi-Turn from 39.38 to 37.99 while retaining overall 64.50. Figure 4 changes the displayed 10-environment BFCL score from 48.1 to 48.0 and 100-environment tau2 score from 16.5 to 16.6. Most retained results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The POMDP formulation, reward equation, history-truncation formulation, and optimization equations are unchanged. No theorem, proof, or substantive mathematical derivation is added or revised; the new reliability and similarity measures serve empirical evaluation.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain an open synthesis pipeline, 1,000 executable environments, and out-of-distribution generalization. A limited novelty-claim broadening occurs in Section 2: v1's 'largest open-source tool-use environment set' becomes 'largest open-source environment set' in v3.

C2.justification: v3 adds interpretations concerning generator independence, task difficulty, judge reliability, and implementation diversity. It introduces concrete adversarial, access-control, and sensitive-domain limitations and removes v1's extrapolation to sustained benefits beyond 1,000 environments. Some new interpretations overreach: Table 8's Sonnet results are not monotonically decreasing, and within-judge repeatability does not establish the claimed cross-model agreement.

D1.justification: v3 newly discloses that the 14B model trained for 32 steps, gives the judge-temperature policy, and identifies the AST-comparison implementation and threshold in Appendix B. These are additional reproducibility details, not evidence of a reduced training budget. Existing synthesis prompts, implementation examples, benchmark adapters, hyperparameter table, and project access information are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds the DeepSWE reference and more specific citations supporting its contrast with benchmark-conditioned training. It explicitly relates AWM to learned world models and replaces the copyright-avoidance rationale with avoiding human priors. The broader related-work organization and principal comparisons remain intact.

P1.justification: There are localized abstract, introduction, analysis, and conclusion edits, plus updated correspondence and publication text. Appendix B inserts reliability and code-diversity subsections before the retained case studies. The overall narrative structure, method exposition, and extensive implementation appendix remain largely intact.

P2.justification: v3 substantially expands the empirical displays with tables for difficulty, generator comparisons, judge reliability, and code diversity, including an expanded appendix reliability table. Figure 4 adds the 191-environment group and hatched EnvScaler bars redisplaying Table 4 scores. Existing tables and figures are redistributed and renumbered; most appendix illustrations remain visually unchanged.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, the additional generator tests, difficulty breakdowns, structural diversity checks, and explicit deployment limitations improve validation and transparency. The gain is moderated by weaknesses in the new reliability argument: repeatability does not establish correctness or cross-model agreement, and Table 13's binary-reward description conflicts with retained partial-credit rewards. The additions provide useful evidence without fully resolving these methodological uncertainties.
